title: Add reusable Human Arbitration agent
summary: Added a Human Arbitration agent spec and persistent rules so facts-checked but irreducible judgment calls are routed to humans instead of fake certainty.

phases.label: Web-first intake
phases.notes: Checked NIST AI RMF, OECD AI Principles, ISO/IEC 42001, and EU AI Act human oversight references.

phases.label: Memory bootstrap
phases.notes: Ran memory bootstrap and checked existing human decision inbox and principle guardian anchors.

phases.label: Mode, boundary, and plan
phases.notes: Selected governance mode and scoped the work to agent-platform plus shared instructions/history.

phases.label: Requirements and spec
phases.notes: Added REQ-WS-068, spec artifacts, source provenance, plan evidence, and request trace.

phases.label: Implementation
phases.notes: Added agent config, docs, persistent instructions, README updates, memory anchor, and coordination status.

phases.label: Verification
phases.notes: JSON, inspect-agent, list-agents, orchestration, unit tests, memory bootstrap, config contract, docs/naming/structure audits, workspace index, task board, workspace-monitor collect/test/check/build, and workspace-health passed.

phases.label: Evaluation and rework
phases.notes: Omission, grounding, and evaluate-work checks were prepared and run after verification.

phases.label: Commit and push
phases.notes: Commit and push are performed as the final close-out step after evaluation.

bottleneck_notes: Governance documentation and full validation dominate this agent-only change.
Reusing the existing human decision inbox avoids building a duplicate decision store.
improvement_candidates: After several arbitration packets exist, consider a deterministic packet validator or monitor UI panel.
